title: TestJack: Should you trust the results in coding benchmarks? Agentic Coding Benchmarks Auditing via Evaluator Evolution
title_zh: <TestJack：你是否应该信任编码基准测试的结果？通过评估者演化对智能体编码基准进行测试审计

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly reshaping software engineering, accompanied by an explosion of new code benchmarks. Yet nearly all existing benchmarks still rely on the same decades-old criterion: a solution is correct if it passes a fixed set of unit tests . Such tests are often insufficient: they check only part of what the task requires, so agents can reward hack them or silently miss required behavior while still passing every test. As a result, higher benchmark scores may partly reflect better adaptation to the evaluator rather than better problem solving. Existing works focus on static test augmentation: they strengthen each task’s tests once, before any trial is seen, and thus overlook how real trials actually fail. We introduce TestJack , a scalable framework for evaluating patches beyond fixed tests. For each trial, TestJack generates tests targeting prompt requirements the patch may violate, retains only tests passed by the ground-truth patch, and re-examines any trial failures. Each confirmed failure is thus supported by a replayable test. To reduce evaluation cost, we also introduce a lightweight variant which audits a random sample of trials in depth and reuses the resulting tests across all trials for the same task. Across 6 frontier model backends and 5 benchmarks such as DeepSWE and SWE Marathon, we find that about 34.4% of the model trials currently judged correct violate the task requirements, lowering the overall resolution rate from 50.6% to 33.2%. Our results reveal a fundamental limitation of current coding-agent evaluation: as LLMs become better at optimizing against fixed evaluators, those evaluators themselves must become more adaptive.
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体正在迅速改变软件工程领域，与此同时，新的代码基准测试也呈爆炸式增长。 然而，几乎所有现有的基准测试仍然依赖同一个沿用数十年的标准：如果解决方案能通过一组固定的单元测试，则被视为正确。 这类测试往往并不充分：它们只验证了任务要求的一部分，因此智能体可能会通过投机取巧的方式通过测试，或者在悄无声息中遗漏必要行为，但仍能全部通过测试。 因此，更高的基准测试分数可能部分反映了模型对评估者的更好适应，而非更出色的问题解决能力。 现有研究主要集中在静态测试增强上：它们在任何试验开始前就对每个任务的测试进行一次强化，因而忽略了真实试验中实际出现的失败情况。 我们提出了 TestJack，一个可扩展的框架，用于在固定测试之外评估代码补丁。 对于每次试验，TestJack 会生成针对提示词要求可能存在的违规情况的测试，仅保留基准答案补丁通过的测试，并重新检查任何试验中的失败情况。 因此，每一次确认的失败都有可重放的测试作为依据。 为降低评估成本，我们还引入了一种轻量级变体：它会对随机抽取的试验样本进行深度审计，并将由此生成的测试重复用于同一任务的所有试验中。 在 6 个前沿模型后端和包括 DeepSWE 与 SWE Marathon 在内的 5 项基准测试中，我们发现目前约 34.4% 被判定为正确的模型试验实际上违反了任务要求，导致整体正确率从 50.6% 下降至 33.2%。 我们的研究结果揭示了当前编码智能体评估的一个根本性局限：随着大型语言模型在针对固定评估者的优化方面愈发出色，这些评估者本身也必须变得更加具备适应性。

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM) agents are reshaping software engineering. Modern agents navigate repositories, edit multiple files, run development tools, and iteratively refine their outputs, and systems such as Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot have become integral to research and production, making their rigorous evaluation increasingly important. Code benchmarks have become the standard yardstick for comparing these agents, from function-level synthesis in HumanEval [ 7 ] and MBPP [ 3 ] to repository-level issues in SWE-bench [ 18 ] . Their number continues to grow, with 210 introduced in 2024 and 316 in 2025 [ 5 ] , and score improvements are routinely cited as evidence of progress.
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体正在重塑软件工程。 现代智能体能够浏览代码库、编辑多个文件、运行开发工具，并迭代优化其输出；Claude Code、Codex 和 Copilot 等系统已成为研究与开发中不可或缺的一部分，因此对其严格评估的重要性日益凸显。 代码基准测试已成为比较这些智能体的标准尺度，从 HumanEval [7] 和 MBPP [3] 中的函数级合成，到 SWE-bench [18] 中的代码库级问题。 这类智能体的数量持续增长：2024 年有 210 个被推出，2025 年则有 316 个 [5]，而分数的提升也常被用作进步的证据。

paragraphs.en: Figure 1 illustrates two kinds of benchmark defects behind this gap. With insufficient tests , the tests check less than the prompt requires, so trials that overlook a required case or game the tests still pass. With an underspecified prompt , a behavior is only implied by the prompt, so whether it must be implemented is ambiguous; the ground truth implements it but no test checks it. Only the first is a defect of the trial: TestJack refutes trials for insufficient tests, whereas it attributes the second to the prompt and reports it as a prompt defect without refuting the trial (§ 3.2 ). The resulting overestimation can be substantial: through manual inspection, SWE-Bench+ [ 2 ] shows that excluding patches that passed only because of weak tests or solution leakage reduces one SWE-bench agent’s resolution rate from 12.47% to 3.97%.
paragraphs.zh: 图 1 展示了造成这一差距的两类基准缺陷。 由于测试不足，测试所检查的内容少于提示词的要求，因此忽略必要用例或规避测试的尝试仍然能够通过。 在提示词定义不充分的情况下，某种行为仅被提示词间接提及，因此是否必须实现该行为存在歧义；标准答案实现了该行为，但没有测试对此进行检查。 只有第一种情况属于尝试本身的缺陷：TestJack 会因测试不足而否定相关尝试，但将第二种情况归因于提示词，并将其报告为提示词缺陷，而不会否定该尝试（§ 3.2）。 由此产生的高估可能相当显著：通过人工检查，SWE-Bench+ [ 2 ] 显示，排除那些仅因测试薄弱或解决方案泄露而通过的补丁后，某个 SWE-bench 智能体的解决率从 12.47% 下降至 3.97%。

paragraphs.en: Existing efforts to close this gap sacrifice either scalability or fidelity. Manual audits such as SWE-Bench+ reliably uncover such failures, but they do not scale: expert review must be repeated for every agent, model version, and run. Automated benchmark auditors such as ABA [ 32 ] ask whether a task is fair and remove flawed tasks, which corrects unfairly failed trials but leaves falsely passed ones in place. Test augmentation methods such as UTBoost [ 37 ] and SWE-ABS [ 36 ] produce executable evidence but remain static : they strengthen each task’s suite once, before any submission is observed, so they catch only anticipated failures and fall short of the reward hacking of modern LLMs. PatchDiff [ 33 ] inspects submissions dynamically, but still relies on human effort to decide which divergences are genuine defects. What is needed is a dynamic evaluator that judges each trial against what the task asks for like a manual auditor, and backs every verdict with executable evidence at scale like automated testing.
paragraphs.zh: 现有填补这一差距的努力要么牺牲了可扩展性，要么牺牲了保真度。 SWE-Bench+ 等人工审计方法能够可靠地发现此类失败，但它们无法扩展：必须为每个智能体、模型版本和运行重复进行专家审查。 ABA [ 32 ] 等自动化基准审计器会判断任务是否公平并移除有缺陷的任务，这虽然修正了不公平失败的测试用例，但保留了那些错误通过的测试用例。 UTBoost [ 37 ] 和 SWE-ABS [ 36 ] 等测试增强方法能够生成可执行证据，但仍然是静态的：它们在观察到任何提交之前，仅对每个任务套件进行一次强化，因此只能捕捉到预期中的失败，而无法应对现代 LLM 的奖励破解行为。 PatchDiff [ 33 ] 能够动态检查提交结果，但仍依赖人工判断哪些差异是真正的缺陷。 我们需要的是一种动态评估器：它应像人工审计一样，根据任务要求对每次测试进行评判；同时又能像自动化测试一样，以可扩展的方式为每个判断提供可执行证据。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we present TestJack 1 1 1 Our artifact is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/testjack-C1A7 . , an automated framework that audits the successes reported by coding benchmarks by evolving the evaluator rather than trusting their fixed tests. Our key insight is to separate what a test should check from whether its expectations are correct: a trial should be judged against the requirements stated in the task prompt, and the ground-truth solution, which benchmarks already possess, can serve as an executable oracle that certifies any new test before it is used to judge a trial. Building on this insight, TestJack audits each benchmark-passing trial with prompt-grounded differential testing : an LLM agent reviews the trial against the prompt’s requirements, writes tests targeting the gaps it suspects, validates each on the ground truth, runs it on the trial, and re-judges any failure to confirm a genuine violation of the prompt, so every refutation is backed by a replayable witness test . Because auditing every trial is expensive, TestJack also offers a lightweight approach that first adds oracle-validated tests for requirements each task leaves unchecked, and then audits randomly sampled trials and shares every confirmed witness with all remaining trials of the task. Since trials for the same task often share failure modes, each expensive audit can refute many trials at the cost of cheap test executions.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们介绍了 TestJack 1 1 1 我们的工具可在 https://anonymous.4open.science/r/testjack-C1A7 获取。这是一个自动化框架，通过演化评估器而非依赖固定的测试用例，来审计编码基准所报告的成功结果。 我们的核心思路是将测试应检查的内容与其期望是否正确区分开来：一次尝试应依据任务提示中陈述的要求进行评判，而基准本身已具备的基准真相解决方案，可充当可执行的“神谕”，在用于评判任何新测试之前先对其加以验证。 基于这一思路，TestJack 采用以提示为依据的差异测试方法，对每个通过基准的尝试进行审计：一个 LLM 智能体根据提示的要求审查该尝试，针对其怀疑的漏洞编写测试用例，在基准真相上验证每个测试，再将其应用于该尝试，并对任何失败重新评判，以确认是否确实违反了提示要求，从而确保每一次反驳都有可重演的见证测试作为支撑。 由于审计每次尝试成本高昂，TestJack 还提供一种轻量级方法：首先为每个任务中未被检查到的要求添加经“神谕”验证的测试用例，然后对随机抽取的尝试进行审计，并将所有已确认的见证测试分享给该任务中剩余的每次尝试。 由于同一任务的尝试通常存在共同的失败模式，因此每次昂贵的审计只需少量廉价的测试执行，即可同时反驳多个尝试。

sents.en: In this paper, we present TestJack 1 1 1 Our artifact is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/testjack-C1A7 . , an automated framework that audits the successes reported by coding benchmarks by evolving the evaluator rather than trusting their fixed tests.
sents.zh: 在本文中，我们介绍了 TestJack 1 1 1 我们的工具可在 https://anonymous.4open.science/r/testjack-C1A7 获取。这是一个自动化框架，通过演化评估器而非依赖固定的测试用例，来审计编码基准所报告的成功结果。

sents.en: Our key insight is to separate what a test should check from whether its expectations are correct: a trial should be judged against the requirements stated in the task prompt, and the ground-truth solution, which benchmarks already possess, can serve as an executable oracle that certifies any new test before it is used to judge a trial.
sents.zh: 我们的核心思路是将测试应检查的内容与其期望是否正确区分开来：一次尝试应依据任务提示中陈述的要求进行评判，而基准本身已具备的基准真相解决方案，可充当可执行的“神谕”，在用于评判任何新测试之前先对其加以验证。

sents.en: Building on this insight, TestJack audits each benchmark-passing trial with prompt-grounded differential testing : an LLM agent reviews the trial against the prompt’s requirements, writes tests targeting the gaps it suspects, validates each on the ground truth, runs it on the trial, and re-judges any failure to confirm a genuine violation of the prompt, so every refutation is backed by a replayable witness test .
sents.zh: 基于这一思路，TestJack 采用以提示为依据的差异测试方法，对每个通过基准的尝试进行审计：一个 LLM 智能体根据提示的要求审查该尝试，针对其怀疑的漏洞编写测试用例，在基准真相上验证每个测试，再将其应用于该尝试，并对任何失败重新评判，以确认是否确实违反了提示要求，从而确保每一次反驳都有可重演的见证测试作为支撑。

sents.en: Because auditing every trial is expensive, TestJack also offers a lightweight approach that first adds oracle-validated tests for requirements each task leaves unchecked, and then audits randomly sampled trials and shares every confirmed witness with all remaining trials of the task.
sents.zh: 由于审计每次尝试成本高昂，TestJack 还提供一种轻量级方法：首先为每个任务中未被检查到的要求添加经“神谕”验证的测试用例，然后对随机抽取的尝试进行审计，并将所有已确认的见证测试分享给该任务中剩余的每次尝试。

sents.en: Since trials for the same task often share failure modes, each expensive audit can refute many trials at the cost of cheap test executions.
sents.zh: 由于同一任务的尝试通常存在共同的失败模式，因此每次昂贵的审计只需少量廉价的测试执行，即可同时反驳多个尝试。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate TestJack on five recent agentic coding benchmarks: DeepSWE [ 17 ] , SkillsBench [ 21 ] , SWE-Marathon [ 12 ] , SWE-bench Verified [ 10 ] , and SWE-bench Pro [ 11 ] , the first three of which were built specifically to avoid weak tests. Of 4,487 benchmark-passing trials from frontier models, including Claude Opus, GPT-5.5/5.6, and Gemini 3.1 Pro, TestJack refutes 1,545 (34.4%): roughly one in three reported successes violates a requirement of its task, and the resolution rate over all 8,862 trials drops from 50.6% to 33.2%. paragraphs.en: Coding Benchmarks. Benchmarks such as MMLU [ 16 ] , BIG-bench [ 30 ] , HELM [ 22 ] , and Humanity’s Last Exam [ 6 ] structure progress in AI, yet their reliability is increasingly questioned: test sets contain label errors [ 27 ] , public benchmarks leak into pretraining corpora [ 34 ] , leaderboard practices can distort rankings [ 29 ] , and flaws in agentic task setup or reward design can misestimate performance by up to 100% [ 40 ] ; dynamic benchmarking [ 20 , 9 , 8 ] responds by continually collecting new adversarial examples. Coding benchmarks have evolved from function-level synthesis [ 7 , 3 ] to repository-level issue resolution in SWE-bench [ 18 ] and its successors, which add human validation [ 10 ] , languages [ 38 ] , modalities [ 35 ] , contamination-limiting refreshes [ 39 , 4 ] , and enterprise-grade changes [ 11 ] . Another line authors tasks from scratch, from command-line work [ 24 ] and skill-augmented workflows [ 21 ] to long-horizon engineering projects [ 17 , 12 ] . Nearly all of these benchmarks share one static protocol: a submission is correct if it passes a test suite fixed when the benchmark is released.
paragraphs.zh: 编码基准测试。 MMLU [ 16 ]、BIG-bench [ 30 ]、HELM [ 22 ] 和 Humanity’s Last Exam [ 6 ] 等基准测试为人工智能的发展提供了衡量标准，但它们的可靠性正受到越来越多的质疑：测试集存在标签错误 [ 27 ]，公开基准测试的数据会泄露到预训练语料库中 [ 34 ]，排行榜的实践可能扭曲排名 [ 29 ]，而智能体任务设置或奖励设计中的缺陷可能导致性能评估出现高达 100% 的偏差 [ 40]；动态基准测试方法 [ 20, 9, 8 ] 则通过持续收集新的对抗性样本来应对这些问题。 编码基准测试已从函数级合成 [ 7, 3 ] 演变为 SWE-bench [ 18 ] 及其后续版本中的仓库级问题修复，这些版本增加了人工验证 [ 10]、多语言支持 [ 38]、多模态能力 [ 35]、限制数据污染的更新机制 [ 39, 4]，以及面向企业级的改进 [ 11]。 另一类方法则是从头开始设计任务，从命令行操作 [ 24] 和技能增强型工作流程 [ 21]，到长期工程项目 [ 17, 12]。 几乎所有这些基准测试都遵循一个静态协议：如果提交的解决方案能够通过基准测试发布时已固定的测试套件，则被视为正确。

paragraphs.en: Benchmark Auditing and Test Strengthening. Prior work on benchmark reliability can be organized along two axes (Figure 2 ): whether the evaluator is static , analyzing a task before any submission is observed, or dynamic , auditing the trials that agents actually produce; and whether its verdicts rest on manual checking or automated auditing. Manual audits expose failures that scores conceal [ 2 ] but must be repeated for every new agent and run. Automated auditors such as ABA [ 32 ] and BenchGuard [ 31 ] use LLM agents to flag tasks whose specification, environment, or grader is broken [ 25 ] ; they audit the benchmark rather than individual trials, and their verdicts rest on LLM judgment. Another line strengthens benchmark tests, from amplifying HumanEval’s tests [ 23 ] to generating additional or adversarial tests for SWE-bench, as in UTBoost [ 37 ] and SWE-ABS [ 36 ] , and issue-reproducing tests [ 26 , 1 ] . These methods are static: they build one suite per task before observing any submission, so their tests must anticipate where agents fail and may encode incidental details of the gold patch. PatchDiff [ 33 ] is dynamic, testing agent patches differentially against the gold patch, but only 28.6% of the divergent patches it reviews can be confirmed incorrect and most cannot be judged either way, so deciding which divergences indict a trial still requires manual inspection. TestJack is, to our knowledge, the first automated dynamic evaluator and occupies the automated, dynamic quadrant of Figure 2 : it audits individual trials rather than tasks, derives tests from the task prompt rather than the gold patch, uses the ground truth only to validate their expectations, and backs every verdict with an executable witness test instead of LLM or human judgment.
paragraphs.zh: 基准测试审计与测试强化。 关于基准测试可靠性的早期研究可以沿着两个维度进行组织（图 2）：评估器是静态的，即在观察到任何提交结果之前分析任务；还是动态的，即审计智能体实际生成的尝试；以及其判定依据是人工检查还是自动化审计。 人工审计能够揭示分数所掩盖的问题 [2]，但必须针对每个新的智能体和每次运行重复执行。 像 ABA [32] 和 BenchGuard [31] 这样的自动化审计器使用 LLM 智能体来标记任务规范、环境或评分器存在问题的任务 [25]；它们审计的是基准测试本身而非单个尝试，其判定依据是 LLM 的判断。 另一类方法则强化基准测试，从增强 HumanEval 的测试 [23]，到为 SWE-bench 生成额外或对抗性测试（如 UTBoost [37] 和 SWE-ABS [36]），以及生成问题复现测试 [26, 1]。 这些方法是静态的：它们在观察到任何提交结果之前，会为每个任务构建一套固定的测试，因此其测试必须预先预测智能体可能失败的位置，并可能包含黄金补丁中的附带细节。 PatchDiff [33] 是动态的，它通过对比黄金补丁来差异化测试智能体的补丁，但它在审查的差异化补丁中仅有 28.6% 能够被确认为错误，大多数则无法判定，因此要确定哪些差异表明尝试失败，仍然需要人工检查。 据我们所知，TestJack 是首个自动化动态评估器，占据了图 2 中的自动化动态象限：它审计的是单个尝试而非任务，从任务提示中推导测试而非黄金补丁，仅使用真实答案来验证其预期，并以可执行的见证测试作为每个判定的依据，而非依赖 LLM 或人工判断。

paragraphs.en: A benchmark instance consists of a natural-language task specification P P ( e.g., a GitHub issue), a repository snapshot R R , a ground-truth implementation G G ( e.g., the developer-written reference patch applied to R R ), and a static test suite T 0 T_{0} used by the benchmark to score submissions. Running an agent on the instance produces a trial : a candidate patch s s applied to R R , yielding a submission R ⁡ [ s ] R[s] . A trial is passing if R ⁡ [ s ] R[s] passes every test in T 0 T_{0} . TestJack takes as input the set of passing trials S = { s 1 , … , s n } S=\{s_{1},\dots,s_{n}\} collected across agents and asks, for each trial, whether its passing verdict should be trusted.
paragraphs.zh: 一个基准实例包括一个自然语言任务规范 P P（例如，一个 GitHub 问题）、一个仓库快照 R R、一个真实实现 G G（例如，开发者编写的参考补丁，已应用于 R R），以及一个静态测试套件 T 0 T_{0}，该测试套件用于基准对提交进行评分。 在实例上运行一个智能体会产生一次尝试：一个候选补丁 s s 被应用于 R R，从而生成一个提交 R⁡[s] R[s]。 如果 R⁡[s] R[s] 通过了 T 0 T_{0} 中的每个测试，则此次尝试为通过。 TestJack 的输入是跨多个智能体收集到的通过尝试集合 S = { s 1 , … , s n } S=\{s_{1},\dots,s_{n}\}，并针对每次尝试询问是否应该信任其通过的判定结果。

sents.en: Running an agent on the instance produces a trial : a candidate patch s s applied to R R , yielding a submission R ⁡ [ s ] R[s] .

sents.en: A trial is passing if R ⁡ [ s ] R[s] passes every test in T 0 T_{0} .
sents.zh: 如果 R⁡[s] R[s] 通过了 T 0 T_{0} 中的每个测试，则此次尝试为通过。

sents.en: TestJack takes as input the set of passing trials S = { s 1 , … , s n } S=\{s_{1},\dots,s_{n}\} collected across agents and asks, for each trial, whether its passing verdict should be trusted.
sents.zh: TestJack 的输入是跨多个智能体收集到的通过尝试集合 S = { s 1 , … , s n } S=\{s_{1},\dots,s_{n}\}，并针对每次尝试询问是否应该信任其通过的判定结果。

paragraphs.en: A witness is a concrete, replayable demonstration that the trial violates a requirement of the task, even though it passes the entire benchmark suite T 0 T_{0} .
paragraphs.zh: 一个见证是一个具体的、可重演的演示，表明该试验违反了任务的一项要求，尽管它通过了整个基准测试套件 T 0 T_{0}。

paragraphs.en: There are two obvious ways to search for a witness test, and each fails in a different direction of Eq.( 1 ). (i) Writing tests from P P alone stays within ℬ ⁡ ( P ) \mathcal{B}(P) but raises the classical test-oracle problem: an LLM-written test may encode a wrong expectation, and nothing certifies that a failing trial is actually at fault. (ii) Writing tests from G G alone , i.e., plain differential testing, accepts any test that separates R ⁡ [ G ] R[G] from R ⁡ [ s ] R[s] . Such tests range over all of ℬ ⁡ ( G ) \mathcal{B}(G) , including the incidental choices in ℬ ⁡ ( G ) ∖ ℬ ⁡ ( P ) \mathcal{B}(G)\setminus\mathcal{B}(P) , so they overfit to the ground truth and penalize a trial for not reproducing the reference patch rather than for failing the task. TestJack combines the strengths of both: it writes tests from P P , which the first condition of Eq.( 2 ) enforces, and uses G G as an executable oracle, which the second condition enforces, so that a new test is trusted only if the ground truth passes it. The prompt thus determines what to test, the trial determines where to look for violations, and the ground truth confirms that the test’s expectations are correct.

paragraphs.en: Execution worlds. The agent builds three copies of the repository under the official evaluator: the model world R ⁡ [ s ] R[s] , the reference world R ⁡ [ G ] R[G] , and the null world R R without any patch. The null world reveals which benchmark tests already pass without a fix and therefore verify nothing about the trial.

paragraphs.en: Evidence collection. The agent then examines the trial’s diff along three axes: (i) ghost branches , code paths in the diff that T 0 T_{0} never executes, identified with branch coverage and classified by whether P P requires the behavior they implement; (ii) reward hacking , checked with explicit detectors for hard-coded expected values, special-casing of tested inputs, test-environment sniffing, harness tampering, and stubs behind a tested veneer; and (iii) general defects , including specification violations, robustness, and security issues, prioritized by mutation testing, which exposes behavior that T 0 T_{0} does not pin down.
paragraphs.zh: 证据收集。 随后，智能体从三个维度检查该测试用例的差异：(i) 幽灵分支——差异中 T₀ 从未执行的代码路径，通过分支覆盖识别，并根据 P 是否需要其实现的行为进行分类；(ii) 奖励破解——通过显式检测器检查硬编码的期望值、对测试输入的特别处理、测试环境嗅探、测试框架篡改以及隐藏在受测表层后的占位符；以及 (iii) 一般缺陷——包括规格违反、健壮性和安全问题，并通过变异测试进行优先级排序，该测试能揭示 T₀ 未明确界定的行为。

paragraphs.en: The per-trial audit is precise but expensive: each audit is a multi-step agent session with repeated builds and test executions, and the number of trials grows multiplicatively with the number of agents, models, and repetitions evaluated on a benchmark. Auditing every trial independently is also wasteful. Trials for the same task often fail for the same reasons, for instance when many agents miss the same edge case, so independent audits keep rediscovering the same defects. TestJack reduces this cost with two ideas: it moves part of the audit from individual trials to the task itself, and it shares every validated witness across all trials of the task (Algorithm 1 in Appendix A.3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 每次试验的审计虽然精确，但成本高昂：每次审计都是一个多步骤的智能体会话，涉及反复构建和测试执行；而且试验次数会随着基准测试中评估的智能体、模型和重复次数的增加而呈乘数效应增长。 对每次试验进行独立审计也是一种浪费。 同一任务的试验往往因相同原因失败，例如许多智能体都忽略了同一个边缘情况，因此独立审计会不断重新发现相同的缺陷。 TestJack 通过两个思路降低了这种成本：它将部分审计工作从单个试验转移到任务本身，并将每个经过验证的见证共享给该任务的所有试验（见附录 A.3 中的算法 1）。

With G G as the oracle, a test that fails on R ⁡ [ G ] R[G] is refined using the execution feedback until it passes, or discarded once the refinement budget is exhausted. paragraphs.en: Randomized audit with cross-trial witness sharing. Task analysis cannot anticipate every way a trial may go wrong, so TestJack complements it with per-trial audits on randomly sampled trials whose witnesses are shared with every other trial of the task, exploiting the fact that trials share failure modes. Let T T denote the current test suite, initialized to T 1 T_{1} . Trials that fail any test in T T are refuted, and the remaining trials form the active set A A . The loop then proceeds in rounds: (i) sample a trial s s uniformly at random from A A ; (ii) run the per-trial audit of § 3.2 on s s ; (iii) if the audit confirms witnesses W W , add W W to T T , share W W by executing it on every trial in A A , and refute all trials that fail; (iv) otherwise, mark s s as audited-clean and remove it from A A . The loop terminates when A A is empty or the working budget is exhausted. Sharing is sound because a witness belongs to the task rather than to the trial on which it was found. The first two conditions of Eq.( 2 ), that t t checks a requirement in 𝒬 ⁡ ( P ) \mathcal{Q}(P) and passes on R ⁡ [ G ] R[G] , do not involve s s at all, and the reviewer agent judges them against P P rather than against the trial. Thus, once a witness is accepted, deciding whether it refutes another trial reduces to the third condition.

paragraphs.en: The scheme is economical because generating and validating tests is expensive, whereas replaying a test on another trial costs a single execution. Each audit round pays the generation cost once while its witnesses are shared with the entire active set, so when trials share failure modes, the number of expensive audits approaches the number of distinct defects rather than of defective trials. The trade-off is coverage: shared witnesses are not re-judged for each trial they refute, and defects unique to never-sampled trials can be missed under a finite budget (§ 4.3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 该方案具有经济性，因为生成和验证测试的成本很高，而在另一次试验中重放一个测试只需单次执行。 每次审计轮次只需支付一次生成成本，而其中的见证者则与所有活跃集合共享；因此，当试验之间存在失效模式时，昂贵的审计次数将接近于不同缺陷的数量，而非有缺陷的试验数量。 这种权衡体现在覆盖范围上：共享的见证者无需为它们所反驳的每次试验重新判断，并且在预算有限的情况下，可能遗漏那些仅出现在从未被采样的试验中的独特缺陷（§ 4.3）。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate TestJack along four research questions:
paragraphs.zh: 我们从四个研究问题出发，对 TestJack 进行评估：

paragraphs.en: RQ1 (Per-trial auditing on frontier benchmarks): When the per-trial audit of § 3.2 is applied to every benchmark-passing trial, how many successes does it refute, and how much do the refutations lower reported resolution rates?

paragraphs.en: Benchmarks. We audit five recent agentic coding benchmarks, summarized in Table 1 : SWE-bench Verified [ 10 ] , SWE-bench Pro [ 11 ] , DeepSWE [ 17 ] , SkillsBench [ 21 ] , and SWE-Marathon [ 12 ] . They span the two ways of building the static verifier T 0 T_{0} : tests inherited from the resolving pull request (SWE-bench Verified and Pro), and verifiers written from scratch (DeepSWE, SkillsBench, and SWE-Marathon), the latter designed specifically to avoid weak inherited tests. All five provide the task specification P P , an executable environment R R , and a reference solution G G . For the container-based benchmarks (SkillsBench and SWE-Marathon), G G is the task’s oracle solution, a trial s s is the agent’s final container state, and the hidden verifier plays the role of T 0 T_{0} . We audit every task of SWE-bench Verified, DeepSWE, and the public split of SWE-bench Pro, the coding tasks of SkillsBench, and the SWE-Marathon tasks that need no GPU and are not ultra-long-horizon (Appendix B.1 ).

paragraphs.en: Agents and trials. We audit trials of frontier models, whose scores drive current claims of progress: Claude Opus 4.6/4.7/4.8, GPT 5.5/5.6, and Gemini 3.1 Pro, regardless of the agent harness. For DeepSWE, SkillsBench, and SWE-Marathon, we use the trajectories released by the benchmark authors, covering vendor agents ( e.g., Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI) and open scaffolds ( e.g., mini-swe-agent). For SWE-bench Verified and Pro, which have few open trajectories from these models, we run GPT-5.6-sol with medium thinking effort under mini-swe-agent, with two trials per task. Of the 8,862 trials in this scope, 4,487 pass the benchmark’s own verifier T 0 T_{0} and form the audit corpus (Table 1 ); the remaining trials serve only as the denominator of resolution rates.

paragraphs.en: We run the per-trial audit of § 3.2 on every benchmark-passing trial (Table 2 ). TestJack refutes 1,545 of 4,487 trials (34.4%), lowering the resolution rate over all 8,862 trials in scope from 50.6% to 33.2%; each refutation is backed by a witness test that checks a requirement of the prompt, passes on the ground truth, fails on the trial, and survives re-judgment. Roughly one in three successes thus violates the task requirements despite passing the benchmark’s own verifier. The refutation rate ranges from 7.6% on SWE-bench Verified to 53.6% on SWE-Marathon, and careful verifier design does not remove the problem: the from-scratch verifiers of DeepSWE and SWE-Marathon yield the two highest rates (43.5% and 53.6%). Appendix C presents representative refuted trials.

paragraphs.en: We run the lightweight approach of § 3.3 on DeepSWE, SkillsBench, and SWE-Marathon with a budget of three audit rounds per task and compare it with the per-trial audit on the same trials; SWE-bench Verified and Pro have too few trials per task for randomized auditing. As Table 3 shows, it recovers 72.4% of the per-trial refutations while reducing API cost by 84.6%, to $4,037 in total, with recall ranging from 40.0% on SWE-Marathon to 80.0% on SkillsBench. Witness sharing makes this trade favorable: a witness found on one sampled trial is validated once and replayed on every remaining trial, so the expensive search runs a few times per task rather than once per trial. The disagreement with the per-trial audit mainly reflects underspecified prompts rather than incorrect tests (Appendix B.2 ). The reason why it’s precision is not high is that per-trial auditing keeps each finding attached to one trial which focuses more on the trial itself, while the lightweight approach turns one trial’s findings into an executable gate and replays it on everyone. Thus, the lightweight approach is prone to diffuse the small defects like the underspecified prompts. Moreover, another two limitations follow from the design of the lightweight approach. First, shared witnesses transfer well within a failure mode but rarely across modes, so tasks whose refuted trials span several distinct defects are covered slowly under a finite budget, which we expect accounts for much of the missed 27.6%. Second, uniform sampling spends rounds on clean trials, which hurts most when few trials amortize a round: SWE-Marathon, with 28 passing trials, shows both the lowest recall (40.0%) and the smallest cost reduction (53.7%).
paragraphs.zh: 我们在 DeepSWE、SkillsBench 和 SWE-Marathon 上运行了 § 3.3 中的轻量级方法，每个任务预算为三轮审计，并将其与相同试验中的逐次试验审计进行比较；SWE-bench Verified 和 Pro 每个任务的试验次数太少，无法进行随机化审计。 如表 3 所示，该方法恢复了逐次试验反驳的 72.4%，同时将 API 成本降低了 84.6%，总成本为 4,037 美元，召回率在 SWE-Marathon 上的 40.0% 到 SkillsBench 上的 80.0% 之间。 见证共享使这种权衡变得有利：在一个抽样试验中发现的见证只需验证一次，然后在所有剩余试验中重复使用，因此昂贵的搜索在每个任务中只需运行几次，而不是每次试验都运行一次。 与逐次试验审计的差异主要反映了提示定义不足，而非测试错误（附录 B.2）。 其精确度不高的原因在于，逐次试验审计将每个发现始终关联到单个试验，从而更关注该试验本身；而轻量级方法则把一个试验的发现转化为可执行的门控机制，并在所有试验中重复使用。 因此，轻量级方法容易扩散诸如提示定义不足之类的小缺陷。 此外，轻量级方法的设计还带来了另外两个局限性。 首先，共享的见证在同一故障模式内可以很好地传递，但很少跨模式传递；因此，在预算有限的情况下，那些被反驳的试验涉及多个不同缺陷的任务会被缓慢覆盖，我们预计这解释了大部分缺失的 27.6%。 其次，均匀抽样会将审计轮次分配给干净的试验，当少数试验需要分摊一轮审计时，这种影响最为显著：SWE-Marathon 有 28 个通过的试验，其召回率最低（40.0%），成本削减幅度也最小（53.7%）。

paragraphs.en: We compare TestJack with SWE-ABS [ 36 ] , which strengthens each task’s suite before any submission is observed by combining coverage-driven test generation with adversarial tests that reject mutants of the gold patch. We run SWE-ABS (without cost budget) on DeepSWE, SkillsBench, and SWE-Marathon with the same model as TestJack , replay its suite on the RQ1 corpus, and count a trial as refuted if it fails any added test. As Table 4 shows, SWE-ABS refutes 248 trials (8.5% of benchmark-passing trials) and recovers 9.9% of the per-trial audit’s refutations, against 1863 trials (63.6%) and 72.4% recall for the lightweight approach: a 7.3 × \times difference in recall at comparable precision (50.4% vs. 49.2%). The gap widens as tasks grow more complex; on SWE-Marathon, SWE-ABS refutes no trial at all, while the lightweight approach refutes 10 of 28. Two design differences explain the gap. First, SWE-ABS never observes a submission, so its tests must anticipate where agents go wrong, whereas TestJack targets defects that depend on how a particular trial is implemented. Second, SWE-ABS derives expectations from the gold patch rather than the prompt, so its tests can penalize implementation choices the prompt leaves open ( e.g., exact error messages), whereas TestJack grounds every test in the prompt and re-judges failures. Static test augmentation is thus insufficient, and dynamic trial auditing is necessary to reach implementation-dependent defects.

paragraphs.en: We present TestJack , an automated framework that audits the successes reported by coding benchmarks by evolving the evaluator rather than trusting the fixed tests shipped with them. TestJack audits each benchmark-passing trial with prompt-grounded differential testing: it writes tests for the requirements of the task prompt, certifies each test against the ground-truth solution, and re-judges every failure against the prompt, so that each refutation is backed by a replayable witness test. Its lightweight variant combines prompt-based task analysis with randomized trial auditing and reuses validated tests across all trials of a task. On 4,487 benchmark-passing trials of frontier agents across five benchmarks, TestJack refutes 34.4% of them, including 43.5% on DeepSWE, whose verifiers were written specifically to avoid weak tests, and lowers the overall resolution rate from 50.6% to 33.2%. The lightweight variant recovers 72.4% of these refutations at 15.4% of the cost, with 7.3 × \times the recall of the benchmark augmentation method SWE-ABS. These results suggest that fixed test suites substantially overstate the capability of frontier coding agents, and that evaluators should evolve with the submissions they judge.

Task authors routinely omit requirements they expect any reader to infer, following the maxim of quantity [ 15 , 14 ] , much as customers never state the “must-be” features they take for granted [ 19 ] . paragraphs.en: Skipping is not the same as ambiguity. Agents may recognize an implicit requirement and still skip it, since test-based rewards give no credit for untested behavior and agent harnesses often instruct agents to make minimal changes [ 13 ] . Models may also collapse onto the same misreading of a task [ 28 ] . The ambiguous class can therefore contain requirements that are clear but widely skipped. We report the tasks with such ambiguity in Appendix B.2 together with some cases studies.
paragraphs.zh: 跳过与模棱两可并非同一回事。 智能体可能会识别出某个隐含要求，但仍然选择跳过它，因为基于测试的奖励不会对未经测试的行为给予任何认可，而智能体框架通常也会指示智能体只做最小的改动 [ 13 ] 。 模型也可能最终对任务产生相同的误读 [ 28 ] 。 因此，模棱两可类别可能包含那些表述清晰但被广泛跳过的要求。 我们在附录 B.2 中报告了具有此类模糊性的任务，并附上了一些案例研究。

paragraphs.en: Benchmarks. This section expands the summary of § 4.1 . SWE-bench Verified [ 10 ] is the human-screened, 500-task subset of SWE-bench [ 18 ] and remains the de facto standard for agentic coding evaluation. Its tasks are mined from merged pull requests in 12 Python repositories and graded by the tests shipped with each pull request. SWE-bench Pro [ 11 ] follows the same mining recipe on copyleft-licensed repositories, targeting larger multi-file changes and grading with human-reviewed fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests. We use its public split of 731 tasks across 11 repositories, the only split whose reference patches are released. DeepSWE [ 17 ] (version 1.0) instead authors 113 original tasks from scratch across 91 repositories and five languages, and grades them with hand-written functional verifiers intended to accept any implementation of the requested behavior. SkillsBench [ 21 ] and SWE-Marathon [ 12 ] (version 1.0) are containerized, Harbor-style benchmarks whose tasks each ship an instruction, a starter environment, a held-out reference (oracle) solution, and a hidden verifier; SWE-Marathon further hardens its verifiers with multi-layer checks and adversarial exploit search.

paragraphs.en: We apply the requirement classification of Appendix A.2 to the witness tests produced by the lightweight approach. A requirement is ambiguous when the prompt does not state it and most models with passing trials on the task skip it, and we call a task’s prompt underspecified when at least one of its requirements is ambiguous. paragraphs.en: Case 1: textual-richlog-follow-state . The task asks Textual’s Log and RichLog widgets to preserve the user’s viewport after the user scrolls away from the newest entries, and introduces an is_following_end flag, a follow_end() method, and a FollowChanged message. The prompt states that “while auto_scroll is enabled, new writes should follow only when the widget is already following the end”, but it never defines what is_following_end denotes. Two readings remain available. Under a position reading, the flag is true whenever the viewport is at the end, and auto_scroll separately decides whether new writes scroll the view. Under an effective-follow reading, the flag is true only when automatic following is enabled and the viewport is at the end. The readings agree whenever auto_scroll is enabled and diverge only when it is disabled, which is precisely the case that the qualifier “while auto_scroll is enabled” leaves open. The reference adopts the effective-follow reading: it initializes the flag from auto_scroll and refreshes it as auto_scroll and is_vertical_scroll_end . The witness test mounts an empty Log(auto_scroll=False) and RichLog(auto_scroll=False) and expects both flags to be False . All 30 audited trials instead adopt the position reading, report True , and fail. The failure occurs before any content is written, so it concerns only the meaning of the flag and not the scrolling behavior that the task is about. The official tests check the initial state only with auto_scroll enabled, where both readings produce the same result.
paragraphs.zh: 案例 1：textual-richlog-follow-state。 该任务要求 Textual 的 Log 和 RichLog 组件在用户滚动离开最新条目后保留用户的视口，并引入了 is_following_end 标志、一个 follow_end() 方法以及一个 FollowChanged 消息。 提示说明：“当 auto_scroll 启用时，新内容仅在组件已经跟随末尾时才会被跟随”，但从未定义 is_following_end 的具体含义。 仍有两种解读可用。 在位置解读下，只要视口位于末尾，该标志即为 true；而 auto_scroll 则单独决定新内容是否会使视口滚动。 在有效跟随解读下，仅当自动跟随已启用且视口位于末尾时，该标志才为 true。 当 auto_scroll 启用时，这两种解读一致；仅在 auto_scroll 禁用时才会产生分歧，而这正是“当 auto_scroll 启用时”这一限定语所留下的未明确情况。 参考实现采用了有效跟随解读：它从 auto_scroll 初始化该标志，并根据 auto_scroll 和 is_vertical_scroll_end 的状态刷新该标志。 见证测试创建了一个空的 Log(auto_scroll=False) 和 RichLog(auto_scroll=False)，并期望两个标志均为 False。 所有 30 个经过审计的测试用例反而都采用了位置解读，报告结果为 True，因此均失败。 该失败发生在任何内容写入之前，因此仅涉及标志的含义，而非任务所关注的滚动行为。 官方测试仅在 auto_scroll 启用时检查初始状态，此时两种解读产生的结果相同。

paragraphs.en: Case 2: updo-policy-alerting . The task adds policy-based alerting to Updo. A monitored target enters a down state after a configured number of consecutive failures and recovers after a configured number of consecutive successes, and each evaluation returns a decision that carries the event, the state, and the current counters. The prompt requires that target_recovered be emitted “only after consecutive successful checks” and that every returned decision match the tracker state. It does not specify whether ConsecutiveRecoveries records the streak that triggered recovery or only the progress toward a recovery that has not yet occurred, and therefore whether the counter is reset before the recovery decision is returned. The omission is conspicuous, since the prompt does state when the latency-breach counter resets. The witness test configures one failure to enter the down state and two successes to recover, and inspects the decision returned by the second success. The reference increments the counter, resets it to zero upon recovery, and only then constructs the decision, so it reports ConsecutiveRecoveries = 0 . All seven audited trials emit target_recovered with the correct state, previous state, and reason, but report the completed streak of 2, and fail. Both behaviors yield a self-consistent snapshot of the tracker, and the official tests assert the event, the states, and the reason of the recovery decision but not its counter. Whereas Case 1 turns on two readings of a named piece of state, this case turns on an implementation choice, the timing of a reset, that the prompt leaves entirely to the implementer.
paragraphs.zh: 案例 2：updo-policy-alerting。 该任务为 Updo 增加了基于策略的告警功能。 在被监控的目标出现指定次数的连续故障后，其状态将进入“下线”状态；在出现指定次数的连续成功检查后，目标将恢复正常运行。每次评估都会返回一个决策，其中包含事件、当前状态以及当前的计数器值。 提示要求：target_recovered 必须“仅在连续成功检查之后”才被输出，且所有返回的决策都必须与跟踪器的状态一致。 提示并未明确说明 ConsecutiveRecoveries 是记录触发恢复的连续成功次数，还是仅记录尚未发生恢复时的进展；因此，在返回恢复决策之前，计数器是否会被重置也存在不确定性。 这一疏漏十分明显，因为提示中确实说明了延迟超标计数器的重置时机。 见证测试配置为：一次故障使目标进入“下线”状态，两次成功检查使其恢复，并检查第二次成功时返回的决策。 参考实现会先递增计数器，在目标恢复后将其重置为零，然后才构建决策，因此报告 ConsecutiveRecoveries = 0。 所有七次审计测试均正确输出了 target_recovered 的状态、先前状态和原因，但报告了已完成的两连成功次数，因而判定失败。 两种行为都能生成自洽的跟踪器快照；官方测试仅验证了恢复决策中的事件、状态和原因，而未验证其计数器值。 案例 1 涉及对某个命名状态的两个读取操作，而本案例则涉及一个实现层面的选择——即重置的时机，该提示完全将其交由实现者自行决定。

paragraphs.en: Discussion. In both cases the requirement checked by the witness is implicit, and every model with passing trials on the task skips it, so the classification of Appendix A.2 labels it ambiguous. The cases also show that such gaps are inexpensive to close. For Case 1, a single sentence stating that is_following_end equals auto_scroll and is_vertical_scroll_end , together with an acceptance example for the disabled case, removes the ambiguity. For Case 2, a sentence stating that the counter resets before the recovery decision is constructed, together with the failure-and-recovery sequence above as an acceptance example, does the same. The witness tests that TestJack withholds from refutation therefore remain useful: they pinpoint where a benchmark’s prompt should be clarified.

paragraphs.en: The refutations of the per-trial audit expose defects of the benchmark tests rather than of the tasks themselves. paragraphs.en: The gap generalizes beyond this trial. Three independent failures survive the changed scanner assertion: a migration that is missing, unregistered, or ineffective, which is the defect here; a column that exists while album refresh or repository mapping never persists the generated paths; and a migration that creates the column without requesting the rescan, so albums indexed earlier never receive their artwork. Closing the gap requires assertions at the stages the feature actually spans, namely a schema check after running the production migration path, an album round-trip through the real repository with paths joined by filepath.ListSeparator , and a check that applying the migration requests a full rescan. Such tests must use an isolated temporary database rather than a fixture that creates image_files by hand, since a hand-made column conceals exactly the omission this case exposes, and they must be added to the graded selection: assertions that the evaluator never runs close no gap.

paragraphs.en: Case 2: reward hacking in internetarchive/openlibrary . The task, openlibrary-5069b09e (Python, base commit facafbe7 ), concerns moving a booknote to a different work when the destination already holds a conflicting record. Booknotes carry the composite primary key (username, work_id, edition_id) , so updating a source record to a destination that shares the username and edition violates uniqueness. The fix must prevent the loss of the conflicting notes and return a dictionary of rows_changed , rows_deleted , and failed_deletes . The reference solution sets Booknotes.ALLOW_DELETE_ON_CONFLICT = False and, when a bulk update hits a conflict, falls back to update_work_ids_individually , which preserves each conflicting booknote, increments the failure count once per such record, and still moves the records that can move. Other record types, bookshelves in particular, keep their deletion-on-conflict policy.

paragraphs.en: One qualification belongs with this case. The prompt describes the conflict example as recording “one failure” and asks that booknotes remain completely unchanged in a conflict, wording that a reader could take to license a whole-operation rollback. The literal 1 alone is therefore not proof of deliberate gaming, and the mixed-update and helper witnesses are the ones that establish a genuine departure from the requested behavior. Our verdict is accordingly behavioral: the trial passes by satisfying an insufficient observation rather than by implementing the requested handling, and we make no claim about the model’s intent or its knowledge of the hidden tests. The task would also benefit from stating its contract explicitly, namely that failed_deletes counts conflicting source records, that conflicts preserve both notes, that independently movable notes still update, and that the shared helper respects the booknote policy.
paragraphs.zh: 有一项资格与此案例相关。 提示词将冲突示例描述为记录了“一次失败”，并要求在冲突中书注完全保持不变，这种措辞可能被读者理解为授权对整个操作进行回滚。 因此，仅凭字面意义上的“1”并不能证明存在蓄意的策略性操作，而混合更新和辅助见证者才是确立真正偏离所要求行为的关键。 因此，我们的裁决属于行为层面的：该测试通过满足一项不充分的观察而非执行所要求的处理来通过，我们并未对模型的意图或其对隐藏测试的了解做出任何断言。 该任务若能明确陈述其契约，也将大有裨益，即 failed_deletes 会统计冲突的源记录，冲突会保留所有书注，可独立移动的书注仍会更新，且共享的辅助组件会遵守书注策略。

paragraphs.en: The lightweight approach reaches a verdict for a whole task in two stages: prompt-based task analysis builds the augmented suite T 1 T_{1} and refutes every trial that fails it, and the randomized loop then audits a few sampled survivors and replays the confirmed witnesses on the rest (Algorithm 1 ). We follow one DeepSWE task, httpx-deterministic-cookie-store , through both stages to show what each contributes and why the cheap stage does not subsume the expensive one. The task asks for a public httpx.CookieStore that extracts cookies from responses and builds outgoing Cookie headers, with deterministic ordering and eviction, expiry, domain and path matching, prefix rules, and mapping operations, while leaving existing behavior unchanged unless the new store is used. Of the trials in our corpus, 42 pass the official verifier, whose suite is substantial: it constructs both Client(cookies=store) and AsyncClient(cookies=store) , imports a CookieJar , checks ordinary domain matching, and confirms that an extracted Secure cookie is withheld from an HTTP request. TestJack nonetheless refutes 24 of the 42, as summarized in Table 9 .
paragraphs.zh: 这种轻量级方法分两个阶段完成整个任务的裁决：基于提示的任务分析会构建增强套件 T₁，并驳回所有未能通过该套件的测试用例；随后，随机循环会对少数通过筛选的样本进行审计，并将已确认的见证用例重新应用于其余部分（算法 1）。 我们通过 DeepSWE 的一个任务 httpx-deterministic-cookie-store 来展示这两个阶段各自的作用，以及为何廉价阶段无法完全取代昂贵阶段。 该任务要求实现一个公共的 httpx.CookieStore，能够从响应中提取 Cookie 并构建外发的 Cookie 标头，同时需满足确定性排序与驱逐机制、过期时间、域和路径匹配、前缀规则及映射操作，且在不使用新存储器的情况下保持原有行为不变。 在我们语料库中的测试用例里，有 42 个通过了官方验证器。该验证器的套件相当庞大：它同时构建了 Client(cookies=store) 和 AsyncClient(cookies=store)，导入了一个 CookieJar，检查了常规的域匹配逻辑，并确认了提取出的 Secure Cookie 不会被包含在 HTTP 请求中。 尽管如此，TestJack 仍驳回了这 42 个测试用例中的 24 个，具体结果汇总于表 9。

paragraphs.en: What the two stages contribute. Replaying the four audit-generated witnesses on the 31 survivors refutes 13 further trials, so the loop’s three expensive audits transfer to more than four times as many trials as they inspect. Of the 42 trials the benchmark accepts, 24 (57.1%) are refuted, 11 by task analysis and 13 by the randomized loop, and 18 survive. The two stages find different kinds of defects. Task analysis finds requirements that the prompt enumerates and T 0 T_{0} leaves unchecked, which is why its tests are cheap to derive and refute trials in bulk. The randomized loop finds defects that live inside implementation choices, namely a normalization helper that widens acceptance, a setter that silently drops metadata, and a scheme predicate with one extra entry, none of which is visible from the prompt and the official tests alone. Every witness here checks a requirement classified as necessary (Appendix A.2 ), so all 24 refutations stand. The replay result also reflects one execution of the loop: the sampled trials are themselves members of the pool, and a different sample would fix the witnesses in a different order, so the count of rounds needed to reach this outcome is not fixed by this run alone.
paragraphs.zh: 这两个阶段各自贡献了什么。 将审计生成的四个见证在31个幸存者上重新运行，驳斥了另外13次试验，因此该循环中三次昂贵的审计所覆盖的试验数量，超过了它们实际检查数量的四倍。 在基准接受的42次试验中，有24次（57.1%）被驳斥，其中11次通过任务分析驳斥，13次通过随机循环驳斥，另有18次通过检验。 这两个阶段发现了不同类型的缺陷。 任务分析发现了提示中列出但 T 0 T_{0} 未检查到的要求，因此其测试易于推导，并能批量驳斥试验。 随机循环则发现了存在于实现选择中的缺陷，具体包括一个扩大了接受范围的归一化辅助函数、一个静默丢弃元数据的设置器，以及一个多了一个额外条目的方案谓词；仅凭提示和官方测试无法发现这些缺陷中的任何一项。 此处的每个见证都检查了一个被归类为必要要求（附录 A.2），因此全部24次驳斥均成立。 重新运行的结果也反映了循环的一次执行：被采样的试验本身属于该试验池，而不同的采样会按不同顺序处理这些见证，因此仅凭本次运行无法确定达到此结果所需的轮数是否固定。

sents.zh: 任务分析发现了提示中列出但 T 0 T_{0} 未检查到的要求，因此其测试易于推导，并能批量驳斥试验。

sents.en: The randomized loop finds defects that live inside implementation choices, namely a normalization helper that widens acceptance, a setter that silently drops metadata, and a scheme predicate with one extra entry, none of which is visible from the prompt and the official tests alone.
sents.zh: 随机循环则发现了存在于实现选择中的缺陷，具体包括一个扩大了接受范围的归一化辅助函数、一个静默丢弃元数据的设置器，以及一个多了一个额外条目的方案谓词；仅凭提示和官方测试无法发现这些缺陷中的任何一项。

sents.en: Every witness here checks a requirement classified as necessary (Appendix A.2 ), so all 24 refutations stand.
sents.zh: 此处的每个见证都检查了一个被归类为必要要求（附录 A.2），因此全部24次驳斥均成立。

sents.en: The replay result also reflects one execution of the loop: the sampled trials are themselves members of the pool, and a different sample would fix the witnesses in a different order, so the count of rounds needed to reach this outcome is not fixed by this run alone.
sents.zh: 重新运行的结果也反映了循环的一次执行：被采样的试验本身属于该试验池，而不同的采样会按不同顺序处理这些见证，因此仅凭本次运行无法确定达到此结果所需的轮数是否固定。

paragraphs.en: We summarize the main limitations of TestJack and of our evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 我们总结了 TestJack 以及我们评估的主要局限性。

paragraphs.en: Dependence on a reference solution. TestJack relies on a reference solution to certify every new test, so benchmarks that ship only a prompt and a test suite fall outside its scope. It further assumes that each task is well-formed, i.e., that its tests, prompt, and ground truth are mutually consistent (Appendix A.1 ); tasks that violate this assumption call for repairing the task rather than re-judging its trials.
paragraphs.zh: 对参考解决方案的依赖。 TestJack 依赖参考解决方案来认证每个新测试，因此仅提供提示词和测试套件的标准基准不在其覆盖范围内。 它进一步假设每个任务都是结构良好的，即其测试、提示词和基准答案是相互一致的（附录 A.1）；违反这一假设的任务需要修复任务本身，而不是重新评估其试验结果。

paragraphs.en: LLM-based auditing. The audit and reviewer agents are themselves LLMs, so a refutation is only as reliable as their reading of the prompt. Oracle validation guarantees that every witness asserts behavior the ground truth exhibits, but not that the prompt requires it. This judgment is delegated to the reviewer. Underspecified prompts, whose implicit requirements a reader cannot reliably infer, remain the main source of disagreement between our configurations (Appendix B.2 ).
paragraphs.zh: 基于大型语言模型的审计。 审计和评审智能体本身都是大型语言模型，因此反驳的可靠性仅取决于它们对提示的理解。 神谕验证确保每个见证者所断言的行为都是真实情况所具备的，但并不意味着提示要求如此。 这一判断被委托给评审方。 定义不明确的提示——其隐含需求无法被读者可靠地推断出来——仍然是我们不同配置之间分歧的主要来源（附录 B.2）。

paragraphs.en: Coverage and precision of the lightweight approach. The lightweight approach trades coverage and precision for cost. Each audit round targets the defects of one sampled trial, so defects that are confined to trials it never samples can be missed under a finite budget, and tasks with few passing trials offer little opportunity to amortize an audit across trials. Moreover, the lightweight approach will amplify the noise in trials and the ambiguity in the prompt and diffuse across other unaudited trials, which has negative impact on precision.
paragraphs.zh: 轻量级方法的覆盖率和精确度。 轻量级方法以覆盖率和精确度为代价来降低成本。 每次审计轮次都针对一个抽样试验中的缺陷，因此在预算有限的情况下，那些仅存在于从未被抽样的试验中的缺陷可能会被遗漏；此外，通过试验较少的任务几乎没有机会将审计成本分摊到多个试验中。 此外，轻量级方法会放大试验中的噪声以及提示中的模糊性，并使其扩散到其他未经审计的试验中，从而对精确度产生负面影响。

paragraphs.en: Scope of the evaluation. We audit trials from a fixed set of frontier models and excluded SkillsBench and SWE-Marathon tasks that are not coding tasks, require a GPU, or are ultra-long-horizon projects (§ 4.1 ), so our refutation rates may not transfer to other agents or task types. Recall and precision in RQ2–RQ4 measure agreement with the per-trial audit rather than with a human-labeled ground truth.
paragraphs.zh: 评估范围。 我们从一组固定的前沿模型中审计了试验，并排除了 SkillsBench 和 SWE-Marathon 中不属于编码任务、需要 GPU 或属于超长期项目（§ 4.1）的任务，因此我们的反驳率可能无法推广到其他智能体或任务类型。 RQ2–RQ4 中的召回率和精确度衡量的是与每次试验审计的一致性，而非与人类标注的基准真相的一致性。
